title: The FBI hunts Charlie Parker over his draft call; Charlie Rouse is sent for
summary: Parker is rejected at induction, while Tommy Crump is drafted and Malachi recommends Charlie Rouse as replacement.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: There were a few little side incidents that happened in St. Louis. One day we were rehearsing, and these two White fellows came in to rehearsals, and they called Billy Eckstine over and was talking to him. Finally, Billy beckoned for Charlie Parker to come over. Charlie Parker went over, and this guy... Everybody was wondering what's happening. So this guy flashes a badge. It turned out he's an FBI man. And what had happened, they had been summoned to find Charlie Parker because he hadn't answered his draft call. So Charlie Parker gave him a story that he had been traveling, and the telegram greeting from the President into the Armed Services had not caught up with him yet. So anyway, they agreed that if he would come down to the induction center the next day, that he would be okay.

So he worked that night, and everybody's sad again, because we'd already lost Tommy Crump, or we were getting ready to lose Tommy Crump, and now they're going to take Charlie Parker, you know, and we'd lost Buddy Anderson.

Anyway, the next morning... He was due there at 8 o'clock. Everybody saw Charlie off to go to the induction center. And Charlie went and took nothing but his horn. He left his suitcase and his bags and everything in his room. And everybody's sad all day, until about 4 o'clock that evening Charlie Parker came walking up to the hotel with his horn, and the results were that he had been rejected. So that was a happy occasion.

Meantime, Tommy Crump, the tenor saxophone player, had been drafted into the Army. So I told Billy Eckstine about this tenor saxophone player I knew in Washington whose name was Charlie Rouse. Billy said, "Send and get him." So we sent and got Charlie Rouse, and Charlie Rouse came to St. Louis, and joined the band.
